subject: physics
promptStrong: Give me an exam-style {board} {level} {subject} question on {lo}, then mark my answer against the mark scheme.
promptWeak: Explain {lo} for {board} {level} {subject} simply, with a clear example and the most common mistake students make.

questions.q: Hadrons are particles that:
options: are fundamental and feel only the weak force
questions.explain: Hadrons are composed of quarks and so experience the strong interaction.

questions.q: In a magnetic field, alpha and beta-minus particles deflect:
questions.explain: They carry opposite charges (alpha positive, beta-minus negative) so deflect in opposite directions.

questions.q: Binding energy is the energy:
options: required to separate a nucleus into its individual nucleons
questions.explain: Binding energy equals the work needed to completely separate a nucleus into free nucleons.

questions.q: The number of undecayed nuclei after time t is given by:
questions.explain: Radioactive decay follows an exponential law N = N0 e^(-lambda t).

questions.q: Which of the following is a lepton?
questions.explain: The muon is a fundamental lepton; protons, neutrons and pions are hadrons.

questions.q: In beta-plus decay the exchange particle emitted is a:
questions.explain: Beta-plus decay (p -> n) proceeds via emission of a W+ boson.

questions.q: Which particle has the greatest specific charge?
questions.explain: The electron has a tiny mass yet carries one elementary charge, giving it the largest charge-to-mass ratio.

questions.q: Which of the four fundamental forces is responsible for beta decay?
questions.explain: Beta decay involves quark flavour change mediated by the weak interaction (W bosons).

questions.q: The charge of a down quark in units of e is:
questions.explain: The down quark carries a charge of -1/3 e.

questions.q: The relationship between half-life T-half and decay constant lambda is:
questions.explain: Setting N = N0/2 in the decay law gives T-half = ln2/lambda.

questions.q: The exchange particle of the electromagnetic force is the:
questions.explain: The virtual photon is the gauge boson mediating the electromagnetic interaction.

questions.q: Confirm the proton charge: uud gives a total charge of:
questions.explain: (+2/3) + (+2/3) + (-1/3) = +1, so the proton has charge +1e.

questions.q: When a particle meets its antiparticle they may undergo:
questions.explain: A particle and its antiparticle annihilate, converting their mass into energy (photons).

questions.q: Isotopes of an element have the same number of:
questions.explain: Isotopes share proton number (same element) but differ in neutron number.

questions.q: The quark composition of a neutron is:
questions.explain: A neutron is one up quark and two down quarks (udd).

questions.q: Which is a typical product set of uranium-235 induced fission?
options: Two equal helium nuclei and no neutrons
Two lighter daughter nuclei plus two or three neutrons
questions.explain: U-235 fission produces two unequal daughter nuclei plus 2-3 neutrons and energy.

questions.q: Nuclear fission of a large nucleus releases energy because the products have:
questions.explain: The fragments lie nearer the peak of the curve with higher binding energy per nucleon, releasing energy.

questions.q: In the reaction p -> n + e+ + neutrino, which conservation law confirms a neutrino (not antineutrino) appears?
questions.explain: The positron has lepton number -1, so a neutrino (+1) must be emitted to conserve lepton number.

questions.q: In any particle interaction, the baryon number must be:
questions.explain: Baryon number is conserved in all known interactions.

questions.q: Fusion in stars requires very high temperatures mainly to:
options: overcome the electrostatic repulsion between nuclei
questions.explain: High kinetic energy lets positively charged nuclei approach closely despite Coulomb repulsion.

questions.q: The activity of a radioactive sample is given by:
questions.explain: Activity equals the decay constant multiplied by the number of undecayed nuclei, A = lambda N.

questions.q: Nuclear fusion of small nuclei releases energy because the product nucleus has:
questions.explain: Fusing light nuclei moves up the steep left side of the curve, increasing binding energy per nucleon.

questions.q: The decay constant lambda represents the:
options: probability per unit time that a nucleus decays
questions.explain: Lambda is the probability of decay of a nucleus per unit time.

questions.q: The pion (pi+) has quark composition u dbar. Its baryon number is:
questions.explain: A quark (+1/3) and antiquark (-1/3) give a baryon number of 0, as expected for a meson.

questions.q: Which quantity is NOT conserved in a weak interaction?
questions.explain: Strangeness can change in weak interactions, unlike in strong or electromagnetic ones.

questions.q: The minimum photon energy needed to produce an electron-positron pair is closest to:
questions.explain: Each particle has rest energy 0.511 MeV, so the minimum is 2 x 0.511 = 1.02 MeV.

questions.q: A source has a decay constant of 0.02 per second and 5.0 x 10^6 undecayed nuclei. Its activity is approximately:
On the N-Z stability graph, light stable nuclei lie:
options: close to the N = Z line
questions.explain: Light stable nuclei lie near N = Z; heavier ones need more neutrons (curve above the line).

questions.q: The mass defect (delta m) and binding energy E are related by:
questions.explain: Einstein's mass-energy equivalence gives E = delta m c^2.

questions.q: The fact that R is proportional to A^(1/3) implies that nuclear density is:
questions.explain: Mass is proportional to A and volume to R^3 (i.e. A), so density is roughly constant across nuclei.
